title: Persist-first announce commit burns a sequence number on relay failure for persistent stores
description: Found by correctness+robustness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx. In rpl_stack/receive.rs process_announce (376-407) the staged clone shares the durable store via Rc<RefCell>; staged.process() commits pin+floor before relay (announce.rs persist-first block). If send_l2_payload_to fails, self.announces = staged is skipped but the durable floor is already at seq N; the originator's same-seq retry (the invariant enshrined by failed_announce_relay_can_retry_same_origin_sequence, rpl_stack/tests.rs:753) then hits !seq_gt(N,N) -> StaleSeqNum and receive.rs forget_peer. Ephemeral processors (AnnounceProcessor::new) keep the old retry contract because is_persistent() skips the store, so the tested behavior and persistent-gateway behavior silently diverge. Bounded (next periodic announce advances seq; matches GCP-6.5's 'surviving cached value forces the legitimate sender to increment') but on lossy LoRa relay failures are routine. Decide: document the divergence, or add equal-seq idempotent retransmission for the durable floor (requires replay-amplification analysis since hop_count is unsigned).
